subject: Throughput shortfall — commercial reconciliation & exec review
messages:
From: Peter Lin <peter.lin@amplitech.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: urgent: production throughput drop impacting nightly batching

Connor —

We saw a sustained throughput regression starting ~03:00 UTC on Oct 1 that knocked our nightly batch jobs from 9k qps down to ~4.2k qps for ~18 hours. That caused downstream ETL windows to miss deadlines and triggered retries; we estimate ~2.3M tokens reprocessed and several time-sensitive jobs failed. Our ops team captured token-level traces and are attaching two samples.

This is now in front of our CTO and procurement. We're expecting: (1) a clear RCA, (2) an estimate of customer impact in dollars, and (3) a proposal for remediation or commercial make-good. Please escalate — the impact is material to our quarterly close.

Attaching: throughput samples (CSV) — request this be treated as high priority.

—Peter
Peter Lin
Head of Infrastructure
AmpliTech, Inc.

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Peter Lin <peter.lin@amplitech.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: urgent: production throughput drop impacting nightly batching

Peter — thank you for the signal and the samples. I’m very sorry for the disruption. We’ve opened a Sev-P ticket and our SRE team is already replaying the traces you attached.

Immediate next steps from our side:
- I’ve asked SRE to provide a timeline and an initial impact estimate by EOD PT.
- Customer success will coordinate a sandbox access point so you can validate any fixes before we roll.
- I’ll set up an exec-facing call for tomorrow with our CTO and your engineering leads to walk the RCA and commercial options.

Can you confirm whether the 2.3M token reprocess number is the full scope or a sampling? Also, please loop procurement (procurement@amplitech.com) if you want formal commercial correspondence.

We take this seriously — will be in touch ASAP with a more concrete offer.

Regards,
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: urgent: production throughput drop impacting nightly batching

Team — forwarding the customer's note and the CSV samples. Key asks from AmpliTech: RCA, quantified impact, commercial remediation.

SRE notes so far (summary from initial triage):
- Regression correlates with a model variant rollout in us-west-2 at 02:50 UTC.
- Degradation manifested as 2–2.5x increased tail-latency under peak batch windows; continued for ~18 hours until autoscaler rolled back at 21:15 UTC.
- KV-cache misalignment suspected for long-context jobs; reproducing in the replay.

Commercial implications: AmpliTech is asking for a dollarized impact and is already involving their CTO and procurement. I recommend we:
1) produce an internal impact estimate (ops + finance) by Monday morning;
2) propose a structured fix (model-variant rollback + targeted edge cache warm-up) and a commercial offer that balances a one-time make-good and a contracted SLA amendment to prevent recurrence.

Vanessa — can you draft a range for a one-time offer (service credit vs. immediate refund) and an amendment proposal? Vivek — will need exec alignment on any offer >$50k.

Connor

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: urgent: production throughput drop impacting nightly batching

Connor / team — attaching a short SLA impact summary for AmpliTech (attached PDF) that maps estimated token reprocessing to billable units and a banded commercial recommendation. Highlights:
- Customer reported 2.3M reprocessed tokens (sampled) — estimated billable token value at list rates: ~$68k.
- Recommended commercial approach: tiered service credit + conditional product commitments
  - Option A (conservative): one-time service credit equal to 50% of estimated billable impact (~$34k) + free 2 weeks of premium monitoring + a technical remediation ticket prioritized for 30 days.
  - Option B (conciliatory): one-time cash credit equal to estimated impact (~$68k) + 60 days of waived overage charges and a small SLA amendment to guarantee faster rollback windows.

Notes: procurement will likely push for Option B or higher; if they ask for a larger fixed rebate we can convert some of that into a committed monthly discount over 3 months (e.g., $23k/mo credit offset).

I recommend we avoid an open-ended refund and instead pair any credit with a contract amendment that establishes a joint runbook for model rollouts and a rollback SLA. That reduces repeat risk.

Attaching: SLA_impact_summary_AmpliTech_Q4.pdf (stub)

—Vanessa
Account Director, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 11:33:00 -07:00

Thanks Vanessa — good analysis. A few governance notes from leadership:
- Any one-time commercial concession > $50k requires legal review and Exec approval.
- We should prioritize a structured amendment to the contract (formal rollback SLA + enhanced monitoring) rather than ad hoc cash refunds.
- For customer retention we can be flexible with a blended approach: up to 60% cash-equivalent (service credits) of demonstrable billable impact, remainder converted to contracted credits tied to committed usage.

Operational ask: can SRE produce a short remediation timeline (3 bullets) and confirm whether the regression has been fully mitigated? I want the exec call agenda to include: RCA, remediation plan, proposed commercial options (A/B), and a timeline for contract amendment.

If AmpliTech pushes hard, I’m prepared to approve up to $75k in credits total, but with a mandatory amendment and a 30-day post-remediation audit. Anything above that must come to me and legal.

Vivek
VP, Commercial
Redwood Inference

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Peter Lin <peter.lin@amplitech.com>, Sara Howard <sara.howard@amplitech.com>, procurement@amplitech.com
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 8 Oct 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposal: commercial remediation + rollback SLA amendment (AmpliTech)

Peter / Sara — thank you for your patience while we completed the initial impact and remediation analysis. Condensed summary and our formal proposal below.

What happened (summary):
- A model-variant rollout in us-west-2 interacted poorly with long-context KV cache behavior under peak batching, producing elevated tail-latency between 02:50–21:15 UTC on Oct 1. Autoscaler rollback returned effective throughput to baseline; full mitigation validated by Oct 2 03:10 UTC.

Impact estimate:
- Customer-provided sample and our replay support an estimated 2.1–2.5M reprocessed tokens. At list rates this maps to ~$62k (midpoint).

Our commercial proposal (pick one):
- Option 1 (fast-path): one-time service credit of $37k (≈60% of midpoint estimate) applied to AmpliTech's next invoice + 14 days of proactive premium monitoring and a prioritized remediation ticket (30 days SLA).
- Option 2 (comprehensive): a one-time cash-equivalent credit of $62k + a signed contract amendment that: (a) requires joint rollouts for model-variant changes affecting long-context workloads, (b) adds a rollback SLA with a 2-hour intervention window during scheduled batch windows, and (c) commits Redwood to a 30-day post-remediation audit. Option 2 will be routed through legal/finance for approval.

Conditions and next steps:
- We’ll provide a short amendment draft and a DocuSign link once you indicate Option 1 vs. Option 2.
- If you accept Option 1 we can apply the credit within one billing cycle without legal counter-signature.
- If you elect Option 2, Vivek has pre-approved up to $75k in credits pending legal sign-off; anything above will require Exec review.

I propose a joint exec call Monday at 09:00 PT to walk the RCA and finalize the commercial path. Please confirm availability and preferred option.

Attachments: SLA_impact_summary_AmpliTech_Q4.pdf, throughput_samples_oct01_to_oct05.csv (stubs)

Thanks — apologies again for the disruption. We want to make this right and harden the rollout process so it doesn't recur.

Best,
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
